gen-gf-slackey-fs-paquito: Expressive and chunky, Slackey stretches its letters out with long pauses between them. Paquito, a confident serif, tucks its capitals close to the lowercase and keeps the text approachable beside it.
gen-gf-smythe-fs-rowan: Smythe's terminals never close in, giving the heading a bold, open-mouthed swagger over its tightly strung letters. Rowan's text serif then reads like a friendly novel, brushy and generous.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-epunda-slab: Sniglet keeps a quiet, level beat, its terminals stopping short of curling back in on themselves. And Epunda Slab, a dignified text serif with a visibly gaping c, carries a longer read with tall, rounded forms.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-fauna-one: Commanding in a hushed way, Sniglet draws every stroke like a bent steel rod with no accents of weight. Fauna One, a classic serif, carries a literary tone through a long read, its tall middle band and shallow ascenders keeping lines compact.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-glegoo: Sniglet lays down a distinctive, level beat, with terminals that stop short of curling back in. Glegoo, a refined serif, answers with big counters and wide unclosed mouths that let a long page of text breathe.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-hanuman: Hanuman reads traditional and refined, its high-waisted lowercase and wide-set terminals on s giving a text serif a stately lift. Sniglet's lower, level letters sit above it with a quiet, commanding firmness.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-kadwa: Terminals that stop short of curling back in make Sniglet instantly recognizable, level and quiet. Kadwa, a serif with open-ended curves and a large x-height, feels editorial and classic beside it, taller and more relaxed.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-noticia-text: Distinctive and commanding, Sniglet draws a single-width stroke through every glyph. But Noticia Text, a dignified text serif with big entrances into its curves, settles into a literary pace over many paragraphs.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla, a refined serif, lets its lowercase nearly match the capitals, with an e opened like a pried clasp. And Sniglet feels like neon tubing bent into letters of constant thickness, brighter and more playful beside it.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-pridi: Sniglet holds a quiet, level beat, with terminals that stop short of curling back in. And Pridi, a classic serif with generous space between curve ends and stems, gives small letters that stand proud for steady reading.
